chunks: We did not appoint men as arbitrators,
but we appointed the Qur'an as the arbitrator.
And this Qur'an is merely writing concealed between the two covers,
it does not speak with a tongue,
and it necessarily requires an interpreter.
And men alone are those who speak on its behalf.
And when the people invited us to appoint the Qur'an as the arbitrator between us, we could not be the party turning away from the Book of Allah,
since Allah said, Exalted is He: 'So if you differ over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger.'

key_terms.الْفَرِيقَ الْمُتَوَلِّيَ: The party turning to/devoting oneself to
key_terms.بَيْنَ الدَّفَّتَيْنِ: Between the two covers (of the book)
key_terms.فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى اللَّهِ وَالرَّسُولِ: Refer it to Allah and the Messenger

ai.seo_question: Why did the Imams reject the Kharijites' proposal to arbitrate solely by the Qur'an?
ai.summary: Imam Ali refutes the Kharijites' literalist demand for 'arbitration by the Qur'an' by distinguishing between the text itself and its necessary human interpreter, asserting that the silent scripture requires the living voice of the Ahl al-Bayt to be applied. This establishes the theological basis for the Imamate as the indispensable 'translator' (tarjuman) of divine law, ensuring that returning to the Book inherently means returning to the Prophet's authoritative interpretation.
